key_insight: SolCloudLLM combines sky images with time-series in a bidirectional multimodal LLM framework to improve short-term PV and GHI forecasting, especially when clouds drive rapid irradiance changes.
engineering_relevance: Better cloud-aware forecasts can support more reliable PV dispatch, reserve scheduling, and grid operations at sites with limited local training data.
method: Align sky-image patches with time-series patches.
Fuse both modalities bidirectionally into a unified representation.
Map the fused embedding into an LLM for forecasting.
evidence_signal: On the SIRTA and SKIPP'D datasets, the method outperformed the best baselines on MSE across all horizons, with up to 25.4% relative MSE reduction, and showed strongest gains under cloudy conditions and few-shot settings.
watch_item: The approach depends on site-specific sky imagery and careful multimodal alignment, which may limit deployment where camera data are sparse, noisy, or unavailable.
paper_title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
